messages:
ryan_ops: Heads up — started a kernel+driver rebase rollout (kernel 6.2 + NVIDIA 550.36) to us-west-2 ampere pools, and we're seeing NVLink negotiation failures. Affected hosts falling back to PCIe for GPU-GPU traffic, multi-GPU jobs 3-4x slower.

maria_infra: ugh. any logs yet? can you paste `nvidia-smi topo -m` from an affected box?

ryan_ops: grabbing one now. output looks wrong (expected NVLink between 0/1):

```
# nvidia-smi topo -m
         GPU0    GPU1    GPU2    GPU3    CPU Affinity
GPU0     BUS     PCIe    PCIe    PCIe    0-15
GPU1     PCIe    BUS     PCIe    PCIe    0-15
GPU2     PCIe    PCIe    BUS     PCIe    16-31
GPU3     PCIe    PCIe    PCIe    BUS     16-31
```

ryan_ops: also `dmesg` shows a bunch of nvlink negotiation timeouts and a couple of pci link retrain messages. snippet: `nvlink: link training failure, falling back to non-nvlink path`

sam_kernel: which driver exact version? could be a change in the nvlink/peeraccess handshake in 550.x. 

ryan_ops: driver `550.36` from the rollout image. running `modinfo nvidia | grep version` shows 550.36.

anya_sre: are these hosts in a canary pool or across the whole region? impact on running jobs?

ryan_ops: started with canary (50 hosts), but fast autoscaler pushed more nodes with the image to replace older ones and now 200 hosts are on the new image in us-west-2. Several large training jobs failed with CUDA errors (timeout when trying to do P2P memcpy). Some jobs automatically retried but run at PCIe bandwidth now, so queue blowup.

maria_infra: can you run `nvidia-smi topo -m` on a known-good host for comparison? and `lspci -vv` for the PCIe bridge config?

ryan_ops: good host (old image) shows NVLink between siblings. `lspci -s 3:00.0 -vv` on affected host shows ACS and BAR sizes look identical but there is a PCIe Link Speed change right before the nvlink messages: `Link Training: Retraining (Equalization)`, then `Negotiate: Gen1` briefly.

sam_kernel: that retrain -> Gen1 downgrade smells like a firmware or driver link-training regression. Could also be PCIe ACS policy enforcement causing NVLink secondary paths to be unavailable. Did the kernel change PCIe enumeration flags?

ryan_ops: kernel config diff: we enabled `CONFIG_PCIE_PORT_SERVICE` and bumped `pci=nommconf` in boot args for the new image (wasn't set before). Not sure if that's related but it's a notable diff.

anya_sre: for mitigation, can we pin the driver back to 515 for canary hosts and see if NVLink returns? Need to avoid mass rollback if possible.

deploy-bot: Rolling back driver on group `usw2-ampere-canary` to `nvidia-515.86` requested by @anya_sre. ETA 12m.

tess_perf: FYI perf numbers — when NVLink is down, cross-GPU all-reduce throughput drops from ~60GB/s to ~12GB/s for the 8-way NCCL job we ran. Tokenized cost estimate: that class of job will need ~4x runtime, so cost to customer/opportunity loss increases accordingly.

maria_infra: create a ticket with host list + kernel+driver diffs and include `dmesg`, `nvidia-smi topo -m` for each. Tag firmware team too.

ryan_ops: done — ticket INFRA-1023 with logs attached. rolling driver rollback on canary now, will observe for 30m before broader rollout.

sam_kernel: I'll reproduce locally with a test rig and try to bisection the kernel flag. If I can trigger with `pci=nommconf` or the PCIE_PORT_SERVICE change, we can minimize surface area.

anya_sre: thanks. if rollback on canary restores NVLink, hold the region rollout and mark capacity impacted. I'll notify schedulers to avoid placing big all-reduce jobs on the affected pool. :warning:

ryan_ops: canary rollback succeeded on 18/20 nodes, NVLink back on those. 2 nodes still flaky (firmware mismatch), I flagged them for manual reprovision. Holding full rollout.

maria_infra: capturing SLA impact: currently estimating 15% effective GPU capacity loss in us-west-2 for Ampere types until fix; also increased preemptible pressure region-wide as jobs shift.

tess_perf: tag Finance — rough burn calc: if this holds for 24h, incremental cost ~ $6k due to longer job runtime + scheduling inefficiencies.

anya_sre: good work. next steps: (1) block driver 550.x in region rollout, (2) kernel flag bisection (sam), (3) coordinate firmware checks for remaining nodes (maria), (4) update customers running large NCCL jobs via status page if impact expands.

ryan_ops: I'll update the incident thread and notify on-call for the rest of the fleet. thanks all. :thumbsup:
